direction.name: The contact sheet
direction.idea: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.
direction.composition: The name, or one sentence about the work, sits at display size (6–9vw) across the top of the first screen, and the sheet begins directly under it, still inside the first screen. The first screen opens with three or four short blocks of small text across the top on a 12-column grid (who, what, where to reach them), all at 14–16px, and immediately below, the sheet begins: rows of thumbnails at a fixed height (90–140px) with their natural widths, 6–10px gaps, each project forming a run of four to eight frames preceded by its title in the same small text. The sheet fills the whole page width edge to edge with 16–20px margins. Hovering a run dims the others and shows that project's one-line description in a fixed position. A single enlarged frame may interrupt the sheet once per screen at four times the size.
direction.typography: One face. The name at display size on the first screen; everything else at one text size and one small size; hierarchy below the name comes from position and from a single brighter ink for titles.
direction.colour: Black or white ground, so the thumbnails are the only colour.
direction.imagery: Many images: at least 24 frames to make a sheet. They can be project photographs from the dealt set cropped to mixed ratios, or page captures of the work. Square corners, no captions on the frames.
direction.richness: Density and order. The mass of small images forms a texture; the strict rows keep it calm.
direction.pitfalls: With fewer than about 20 images it looks unfinished; choose another direction. Do not add a big headline above the sheet. On a phone the frames become two per row at a fixed height and each run scrolls sideways. Rows that run past the right edge read as clipped in screenshots and to most visitors: wrap the frames onto the next line, or end each row inside the grid.

hero.name: Lit strip, four corners
hero.blueprint: One near-black field with a single lit band. Four small pieces of text at 14px, medium weight, sit in the corners on 72px side margins and 44px top and bottom margins: the name top-left, one link top-right, one sentence saying what this is bottom-left (max 36ch), the single action as a text link bottom-right. Across the vertical middle runs one horizontal strip of photographs, 34vh tall (about 300px), each at its natural width with 10px gaps and square corners: eleven or more frames in a flex row wider than the viewport, so the first and last visible frames are cropped by the left and right edges. The frame nearest the centre is at full brightness; the others sit at filter: brightness(0.55) and brighten on hover or as they reach the centre. Under the centred frame, aligned to its left edge, its title is set in the same 14px text. The top quarter and the bottom quarter of the screen stay empty and dark. The strip scrolls sideways with overflow-x: auto and scroll-snap; never hijack vertical scroll.
hero.mobile: The strip stays a single sideways-scrolling row but grows to 46vh tall, so one frame and the cropped edges of its neighbours fill the width. The name and the link sit at the top on 20px margins; the sentence and the action stack bottom-left under the strip at 14px. Dark space remains above and below the strip, about 12% of the height each.
hero.headline: None at display size: the name at 14px in a corner and one sentence of up to 60 characters.

type.note: A light grotesque with open, slightly old-fashioned shapes; large headings look airy and the text weight beneath stays easy to read. Suits AI and research products, fashion houses and calm brand sites.

palette.name: Soot and lime
palette.note: A soot-black opening and close bracket white middle sections, all in black, white and grey. Pale lime is the single action colour: every button, and at most one headline set in it on the dark ground.

motion.name: Drag row
motion.description: A row of large items wider than the screen that the visitor pulls sideways: native horizontal scrolling with scroll snapping, the first item aligned to the page margin and the last allowed to run off the edge so the row visibly continues. No carousel library, no arrows, no dots.

sections.name: One-size name columns
sections.blueprint: Pure text at one size. Three columns start on columns 1, 4 and 7 of the 12-column grid, leaving columns 10–12 empty on purpose. Each column opens with a group name in full ink and continues with a tight stack of six to ten capability names in the soft ink, all at 16–17px, regular weight, line-height 1.25, no bullets and no symbols; one blank line separates group name from stack. Hovering a name brings it to full ink and shows a one-line description in a fixed spot: the top of the empty columns 10–12, at the same size. The heading is no larger than 28px; two or three words, alone on column 1, 96px above the columns. Give the section 20vh of empty ground above and below, so the smallness reads as decided. Works on light or deep grounds.
sections.mobile: Columns stack with 40px between groups; text rises to 18px with line-height 1.4 for touch. Group names stay in full ink. Hover descriptions are dropped; each group ends instead with one sentence in the soft ink that sums it up. The heading is 24px, 48px above.

sections.name: Dense masonry sheet
sections.blueprint: A three-line statement at 22px, 30ch wide, sits at the 66% column with 64px of space below it; it is the only large text. Then a dense masonry of about twenty tiles in six columns with 4px gaps and 12px outer margins, built with CSS `columns: 6; column-gap: 4px` and `break-inside: avoid` on each figure. Tile sizes range from 90px squares to one feature tile of 280 by 160px that sits above the first two columns, outside the column flow. Images keep their natural ratios, so column bottoms are ragged. Every tile has one caption line at 12px directly beneath, 6px below the image and 14px above the next tile, in the form name, comma, type. Mix photographs, posters, details and textures. No hover chrome; the sheet reads at a glance and fills the full width.
sections.mobile: Three columns with 4px gaps and 10px margins; the feature tile spans the full width at the top. Captions stay at 12px but shorten to the name only. The statement sits above at 19px, full width and left-aligned.

sections.name: Shallow portraits, small quotes
sections.blueprint: Speakers are shown as wide, shallow crops rather than headshots. A two-word heading at 15px sits in columns 1–2, top-aligned with the frames, not above them. In columns 3–12 three frames sit side by side with 8px gaps at unequal widths (4, 3 and 3 columns), all exactly 110px tall: each is a photograph of the person cropped with `object-fit: cover` to a band across the eyes and shoulders. Directly under each frame, on its left edge, come the name in the brighter ink and the role in the softer ink on one line at 15px, then the quotation at the same 15px over three to five lines, no wider than its frame. Everything shares one type size; hierarchy comes from ink alone. If interview clips exist, each frame can be the poster of its clip, but the section must work with stills.
sections.mobile: Frames go full width one after another, each 84px tall, with its name, role and quotation at 15px beneath and 40px before the next. The heading leads as a plain line at the same size, in the brighter ink, 24px above the first frame.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.
references.media: A contact-sheet wall: one fixed WebGL canvas draws about 84 full-page screenshots of client sites at a single 190px width and their native ratios, every page of each project in reading order. Once scrolled, every screen is about three rows, roughly 48% picture and 52% black, with text under 1% and the labels above each frame, never on it; there is no video.
references.motion: The preloader counts at about 13% a second for some 7-8s while the screenshot textures load, although the document loaded in 1.66s; then the first-row thumbnails rise into their slots in random order and a dark veil lifts. Lenis over a 4440px scroll proxy redraws the fixed wall with no pins or reveals; panel and hover moves use transform .75s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), and pictures fade over 1s ease-out on the phone.

references.name: Oimachi
references.idea: A studio homepage that behaves like a dense dashboard: work, posts, experiments and testimonials tiled edge to edge with 8px gutters instead of spaced-out sections.
references.archetype: other: left statement over media row with posts sidebar
references.hero: Charcoal ground (#181818) with only 8px side margins. Top-left: a round logo, then five tiny black rectangular chips with bold white 13px labels; top-right a contact chip and a theme toggle. The headline starts at the left margin about 160px down: two lines of light grotesk at 52px (3.6vw), tight tracking, with one word in italic serif. From 280px to the bottom edge runs a three-part row: two tall images butted together (each about 535x610px: a hand holding a phone on black, a man in a printed tee) and a 330px sidebar of blog posts, each a bold 14px title, two grey truncated lines and a small-radius thumbnail.
references.type: Aeonik throughout: light 52px for the headline, regular 20 to 24px for mid-page statements, bold 13px for nav chips and post titles, 12px grey captions. Single words switch to an italic serif inside headings. The scale is deliberately small; nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #181818 #070707 #2a2a2a #ffffff #ff4a2b #8a8a8a — Charcoal ground with black chips and white text, unchanged from section to section; colour arrives only through work thumbnails in orange-red, purple and green. A light-mode toggle exists.
references.imagery: Client work as photographs, UI shots, brand graphics and generated explorations; rectangles with 4px corners in tight 4:3 strips and a masonry of mixed aspect ratios, each with a tiny caption.
references.layout: 8px margins and 4 to 8px gutters everywhere. Short three-line statements at about 22px are indented to the 33% or 66% column and act as section breaks between tightly tiled image grids. Text columns stay narrow; images take two-thirds of the width.

sections.description: Rows divided by hairlines, each about 120px tall. The left third holds a small client icon, the name in 12px bold and the sector in grey at the top, with a two-line 11px description pinned to the bottom of the row. The right two-thirds holds three equal 4:3 thumbnails with 4px gaps. Above the list a three-line statement at 22px sits at the 66% column with a text link far right.

A statement at the 66% column introduces a dense masonry of experiments: around twenty tiles in six uneven columns with 4px gaps, sizes from 90px squares to a 280x160px feature tile, mixing screenshots, posters, renders and textures. Every tile has a 10px caption beneath in the form 'Name / Type'. No hover chrome is visible; it reads like a contact sheet.

Two wide video stills side by side, each cropped to a shallow band about 95px tall, showing a person mid-interview. Under each: a black square play chip, a small company icon, then the name in bold 12px and the role in grey. There is no quotation text at all; the testimonial is the video.

Four equal columns headed at 20px, each a list of 11px grey links prefixed by a tiny coloured square icon. Below, a large white circle logo with a black rounded square inside at far left, a two-line 20px question at the 33% column, and a small white booking chip with email and phone set inline beside it.

steal: Shrink page margins and gutters to 8px and tile media edge to edge so a portfolio reads as a working dashboard rather than a brochure.
Put a live blog or news sidebar inside the hero next to the showreel, so the first screen proves the studio is active.
Style nav links as tiny solid rectangular chips sitting directly in the page corner instead of in a bar.
references.media: A muted, looping reel of brand work covers about 51% of the first screen (75% of the width, 68% of the height) in a black well beside a rail of three 16:9 news thumbnails. Below: third-split rows with a label column on the left and three 3:2 tiles on the right two thirds, half-and-half video testimonials, an 8-column masonry of mixed ratios with small captions, and a text panel beside a photo stack; 34 images and 17 videos, client work supplying all the colour on near-black.
references.motion: There is no preloader and only the reel cuts after 400ms; a single ScrollTrigger scrubs the news rail at 0.8 so it drifts as the hero leaves, with no smooth-scroll library and no pins. Cards grow an outline over 0.5s on an ease-out-quint, images move over 0.6-0.8s on cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), links fade colour over 0.2s, and 33 skeleton shimmers (1.2s) hold space while media loads, with no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Serotoninn
references.idea: A torn-paper seam splits the page in two, colour on white against greyscale on grey paper, to stage the brand's glam-versus-grunge line, with ultra-condensed heavy type straddling the tear.
references.hero: The viewport is split by a vertical torn-paper edge at 50%: left half pure white, right half a grey paper texture. A cut-out model stands dead centre, about 28% wide, running from 15% down off the bottom edge; her left half is full colour, her right half greyscale, the tear passing through her. Type is ultra-condensed heavy uppercase: the brand name at about 5.5vw top-left beneath a three-line mono menu; a two-line tagline right-aligned at mid-height on the right; and at bottom centre a two-word line at 8.2vw, first word red and second white, overlapping the dress, with a bracketed link beneath. Small centred logo at top, three mono links top-right.
references.type: Thunder extra-bold in uppercase, set tight, for all display lines (118px in the hero, similar for category words, sometimes rotated 90 degrees). PP Fraktion Mono uppercase at about 11px for nav, labels and prices; Inter for small body. Square brackets and parentheses wrap secondary words and counts.
references.colour: #fdfdfd #d8d8d8 #0a0a0a #e8352b #fff9f7 #2a2fb0 — White, paper grey and black with red as the single interface accent (one headline word, section labels). Garment colour (cobalt, yellow, satin tan) supplies the rest. One full black campaign band.
references.imagery: Studio fashion photography of models, cut out or on white seamless, in tall portrait crops. The hero splits one image into colour and greyscale along a torn-paper edge, and the torn edge returns as a divider over the footer video.
references.layout: About 2.5% margins. Sections carry red numbered mono labels at top-left. The layout changes every time: a label column with a product trio; a full-bleed black video; a horizontal row of tall category cards; a two-up split with a torn seam; a footer laid over video.

sections.description: New arrivals. The left 25% is a nearly empty column holding only a red numbered mono label at top, a bracketed link, and two tiny parenthesised notes further down. The right 60% holds three product images side by side with 4px gaps, each about 3:4, the middle one a tight crop of the same garment. Two carry a black brush-stroke tag with white condensed text in the top-left corner. Name and price sit under each in mono.

Categories as a horizontally scrolling row of five tall white cards, about 2:3 with 8px gaps, each showing a full-length cut-out model. The category name is set in the heavy condensed face rotated 90 degrees, running up the card's left edge from the bottom; a bracketed item count sits bottom-right in mono. The fifth card is cropped by the viewport edge.

Two-up split filling the viewport: two half-width photos of models on pale grounds, divided by a vertical torn-paper edge instead of a straight line. Each half has a category word in heavy condensed type at about 3.5vw bottom-left with a smaller parenthesised word attached like a suffix, and a bracketed count bottom-right.

A dark campaign video is cut off by a horizontal torn-paper edge, below which a taupe-grey ground holds the footer. Mono link clusters sit top-left and top-right. A cut-out model stands about 40% across, overlapping a very large condensed wordmark in darker grey so that letters pass behind her. Bottom-left, a subscribe line in white condensed type with a bracketed suffix; an underlined email field at right.

steal: Split one photograph along a torn-paper edge into a colour half and a greyscale half on different grounds, and let a two-word headline change colour across the same seam.
Run category names in heavy condensed type rotated 90 degrees up the edge of tall product cards, with a bracketed item count in mono at the opposite corner.
Reuse a torn-paper edge as the divider between sections and over the footer instead of straight lines.
